transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Time: 11:00 AM PT / 19:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jamie Lee (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood CSM); Priya Singh (Orion, Head of ML), Daniel Cho (Orion, CTO), Sara Patel (Orion, Data Engineer), Alex Moreno (Orion, Product)

Summary:
Quick sync on weekly POC results: prompt-set v1 -> v2 diff, quality regressions observed on 'financial-extract' and 'policy-qa' tasks, discussed scoring thresholds and guardrail additions, decided to run dedicated perf job and share updated benchmark spreadsheet + failure cases.

Topics:
- Regression breakdown (precision/recall, hallucination rate)
- Prompt-set updates and guardrails (negative examples, stricter stop tokens)
- Scoring pipeline changes (reranker thresholds, embed similarity)
- Next steps: benchmarks, perf run, docs/security asks

Transcript:
00:00 Jamie Lee: hey everyone, thanks for sticking to time, we'll kick off, um, quick roll call.
00:06 Priya Singh: hey hi, priya here.
00:08 Daniel Cho: daniel on from here. audio's fine.
00:12 Sara Patel: sara, all good.
00:16 Jamie Lee: great, so agenda  we wanted to go through the quality eval from last week's batch, call out regressions, and propose prompt-set v2 and guardrails. Marco will start with the metrics.
00:30 Marco Diaz: yeah thanks jamie. ok so we ran the 3k prompt sweep  same seed sets as last week  and compared v1 (baseline) and v2 (with few-shot context changes and stop token tweaks). overall f1 on our labelled set is up 2 points but two tasks show regressions: financial-extract and policy-qa. hallucination rate for policy-qa rose from 4.1% to 7.9% on random sample.
00:58 Priya Singh: ugh that's unfortunate, the policy stuff is sensitive. can you give an example?
01:10 Marco Diaz: sure, here's a paraphrase  prompt about refund policy, model invented a clause that doesn't exist, so it's a false positive. looks like the few-shot examples biased it toward over-confident extraction for ambiguous wording. transcribed note: overconfidence -> k-v cash mismatch on prefix caching maybe? (laugh)  i mean KV cache effects on prefix repetition.
01:35 Daniel Cho: is this more a model issue or our prompt design? i know you said v2 added more few-shots.
01:42 Marco Diaz: mostly prompt design; v2 added three in-context examples that were slightly pathologic for short policy excerpts. Also the reranker threshold was lowered to increase recall which trades off precision. so combined effect.
02:00 Jamie Lee: to be explicit  we saw recall up ~6% which helps the extraction coverage, but precision drop on two enterprise-critical flows. that's why we want to add guardrail rules and stronger reranker rules for those routes.
02:18 Priya Singh: sounds right. what guardrails are you proposing?
02:22 Marco Diaz: two layers: 1) prompt-level negative examples  we add examples that show incorrect extraction and say 'don't extract if...' and 2) post-run classifier/reranker tweaks  increase similarity threshold and add a conservative fallback to structured response 'insufficient information'. also consider using Redwood Optimize suggestions for dynamic thresholds per route.
02:47 Sara Patel: can the reranker be biased per-customer? like stricter thresholds for policy-qa but looser for summarization?
02:54 Marco Diaz: yes, route-level thresholds are configurable; you can pin per-route threshold in the config. for Hosted we usually recommend slightly looser defaults; for Dedicated/VPC customers you can set tighter SLOs.
03:10 Alex Moreno: quick question on metrics: how are you measuring hallucination rate? is it manual or automated?
03:16 Marco Diaz: currently it's semi-automated: a seeded human-labeled holdout combined with fuzzy-match heuristics and embedding similarity; for scale we flag low-similarity answers for manual review. we compute hallucination as percent of responses with no matching ground-truth and failing similarity > .65.
03:38 Priya Singh: OK, we need a lower bound on false positives for compliance. ideally <2% for policy-qa. can you get us there?
03:46 Jamie Lee: we can aim for it  Marco will prototype guardrail templates and a stricter reranker threshold to target <2% false positives; tradeoff will be lower recall. we'll document tradeoffs.
04:00 Daniel Cho: on latency/cost  you mentioned reranker adds an extra embedding call, that will increase per-request cost. what's the expected delta?
04:10 Marco Diaz: good call. embedding-based reranker adds ~30-50ms and ~0.5-1.2c per request depending on batch. Redwood Optimize suggests batching embedding evals and prefix caching to amortize. We can run a dedicated perf job on Redwood Dedicated to get real numbers for your workload.
04:32 Sara Patel: we'll need that perf job  our traffic shape is spiky at end of month, 10k req/day with 20% burst.
04:40 Jamie Lee: noted, we'll schedule a dedicated run. Lina will coordinate.
04:46 Lina Park: yes i'll follow up on scheduling and infra details.
04:50 Priya Singh: security question  are these reranker logs stored? we need auditability and to ensure PII is redacted.
04:58 Marco Diaz: logs can be configured. for Private/Dedicated customers you can control log retention and enable KMS-managed encryption. we also offer token-level cost/latency breakdown in Redwood Console. for PII redaction we have integration with post-processing filters and you can route logs to your SIEM.
05:18 Daniel Cho: do you support SSO/SAML and SOC2?
05:21 Jamie Lee: yes, SOC2 Type II in vault, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC controls and audit logs. we'll share the security pack.
05:30 Alex Moreno: another gotcha  we saw one regression on financial-extract where amounts with parentheses were mis-read. is that a tokenizer problem?
05:40 Marco Diaz: could be tokenization or prompt example coverage; parentheses and currency symbols sometimes cause truncation in heuristic extractor. we'll add negative and positive examples for parentheses and ambiguous currency formats.
05:55 Priya Singh: will you also create a whitelist/blacklist for sensitive fields?
05:58 Marco Diaz: yes we can add field-level guardrails, and also a quick post-check to verify numeric parse with regex and confidence threshold. if confidence low, return 'needs human review'.
06:12 Jamie Lee: ok let's talk about scoring pipeline changes. we lowered the reranker score threshold last week to bump recall; for v2 we propose conditional thresholds: if route==policy-qa then threshold=.78 else threshold=.65. we also propose adding a second-stage classification with a smaller model for safety.
06:35 Sara Patel: what's the runtime impact for two-stage classification?
06:38 Marco Diaz: extra latency but you can run second stage async for non-blocking flows or set it to run only on borderline cases. Redwood supports asynchronous callbacks and background evaluation.
06:52 Priya Singh: i'd prefer we keep mainline sync for critical flows and async for others.
06:56 Jamie Lee: agreed. Marco will include synchronous failover options in the docs.
07:10 Marco Diaz: on the prompt-set v2  we've attached a link in the workspace (note: link shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/sandbox/prompt-sets/orion/v2)  the main changes: 3 few-shot swaps, added negative examples, and an extra stop token pattern for policy-qa. i did see one side-effect where the model repeated the stop token phrase  minor but we want to catch it.
07:35 Priya Singh: can you put the prompt examples inline in the spreadsheet? our engineers prefer one-file.
07:40 Jamie Lee: will do. i'll send updated spreadsheet.
07:45 Daniel Cho: are there concerns about model drift over time? how do we detect regressions automatically?
07:50 Marco Diaz: Redwood has quality monitoring  you can attach prompt sets and golden labels; we run continuous regression checks and alert on metric shifts beyond thresholds. we can wire your eval set to the monitors and create a weekly report.
08:06 Sara Patel: great, set that up. also we want a channel for urgent regressions.
08:10 Lina Park: we'll set up a slack channel and configure pager duty if you'd like.
08:15 Alex Moreno: anything on cost optimizations? we still see cost a bit high on burst.
08:19 Marco Diaz: two levers: 1) batching policies for non-low-latency routes and 2) quantized model variant for Dedicated to cut token cost. Redwood Optimize recommended quantization for summarization flows; we can run evals to ensure quality delta is acceptable.
08:39 Priya Singh: ok let's schedule quantization eval after the guardrails are in.
08:43 Jamie Lee: noted. final recap: Marco will prepare guardrail templates + updated prompt-set v2 and push to the sandbox; Jamie will send benchmark spreadsheet and permission link; Lina will schedule Dedicated perf run; Sara will export failure cases. everyone to run regression checks and reconvene next week.
09:05 Priya Singh: that works, thanks.
09:08 Jamie Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc bundle and next meeting invite. bye.

Post-meeting Notes (auto):
- Shared links: prompt-set v2 sandbox link (redwood), benchmark spreadsheet (link in CRM), security pack (link to S3)
- Suggested immediate changes: (1) raise reranker threshold for policy-qa to .78, (2) add negative examples for policy extraction in prompt-set, (3) add numeric parse regex post-check for financial-extract.

End of transcript.
